subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Early Pregnancy Signs: Hegar, Chadwick and Goodell

steps.tx: Softening and compressibility of the lower uterine segment on bimanual examination is the **Hegar sign**. It appears at six to eight weeks as the isthmus softens under hormonal influence. Modern practice relies on urine testing and ultrasound instead. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: The Hegar sign softens the lower uterine segment at six to eight weeks of pregnancy.

steps.tx: Bluish discoloration of the vagina and cervix from increased vascularity is the **Chadwick sign**. It appears around eight to twelve weeks of pregnancy. Other causes of pelvic congestion can mimic it, so it stays suggestive rather than diagnostic. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: The Chadwick sign blues the vagina from vascularity around eight to twelve weeks.

steps.tx: Softening of the cervix to the consistency of lips is the **Goodell sign**. The non pregnant cervix feels like the tip of the nose by comparison. It develops by about six weeks under progesterone influence. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The Goodell sign softens the cervix to lip consistency by about six weeks.

steps.tx: Every modern pregnancy diagnosis starts with a **urine pregnancy test** detecting hCG. It turns positive around the missed period and is highly accurate when performed correctly. Very early testing before the missed period can falsely reassure. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Urine pregnancy tests detect hCG and turn positive around the missed period.

steps.tx: Quantitative blood measurement of the hormone is **beta-hCG** testing. Serial values track viability, rising by at least half in forty eight hours in most healthy early pregnancies. Ultrasound location matters more than any single value. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Beta-hCG serial values track viability, rising by half in forty eight hours when healthy.

steps.tx: Irregular contractions of the pregnant uterus felt on examination are **Braxton Hicks** precursors in early form, while palpable intermittent painless contractions appear later. They never dilate the cervix. Confusing them with true labour is common near term. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Painless Braxton Hicks contractions never dilate the cervix, unlike true labour.

steps.tx: Enlargement of the uterus asymmetric at the implantation site is the **Piskacek sign**. One cornu bulges where the embryo implanted in early weeks. It disappears as the sac grows to fill the cavity. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: The Piskacek sign bulges one cornu at the implantation site in early weeks.

steps.tx: Definitive confirmation of intrauterine pregnancy needs ultrasound showing a **gestational sac with yolk sac**. This excludes ectopic pregnancy in most symptomatic cases. A sac without yolk or embryo at expected sizes needs interval rescan. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Ultrasound showing sac with yolk sac confirms intrauterine pregnancy and excludes most ectopics.

steps.tx: Symptoms of pregnancy including amenorrhoea, nausea and breast tenderness are called **presumptive symptoms**. They prompt testing but never confirm pregnancy alone. Objective confirmation always follows with test and scan. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Presumptive symptoms prompt testing but objective confirmation always follows.
